title: Are the diagnostics reported alongside a population adjustment classifiers of its error?
question: Every population adjustment arrives with a panel of numbers beside it: effective sample size, the same figure as a percentage, the largest weight, standardized differences before and after adjustment, a distance between populations. A committee reads them as evidence about whether to believe the estimate, and a widely quoted rule says to worry below an effective sample size of about 30 to 35. Scored as classifiers of realized error, with discrimination and calibration, against known truth and under a declared distribution of analyses, what are they worth?
design: An anchored indirect comparison with a continuous outcome and an identity link, chosen so that the realized error of a linear estimator splits exactly into arm imbalance, transport error and outcome noise, and a covariate diagnostic can be scored against the only component it could possibly know about. 128 cells crossing an omitted effect modifier, a cross-moment modifier that no baseline table could reveal, overlap, source size, how correlated the omitted modifier is with the adjustment set, and a target dispersion ratio that destroys effective sample size while adding no bias where the modifier structure is correct. 4000 replicates per cell, four estimators. Primary results are reported within misspecification strata rather than over a mixture, so no investigator-chosen frequency enters the headline.
estimand: Transported A versus C mean difference in the target superpopulation; the anchored A versus B contrast as a secondary reference
methods_compared: MAIC matching means and standard deviations
answer: They are variance statistics being read as bias warnings. Effective sample size separates the outcome-noise component of realized error at AUROC 0.847 and the transport component, which is the part covariate adjustment exists to remove, at 0.653. At the quoted cutoff of 35 it catches between a quarter and a third of material errors in every misspecification stratum, 0.309 where an effect modifier is omitted and the omission is diagnosable in principle, at specificity 0.926. Three of the panel's members are provably one statistic, since ESS/n = 1/(1+CV^2(w)) exactly and area under the ROC curve is invariant to monotone transformation; a fourth, the post-weighting balance on matched moments, is zero at the solution of the calibration equations and cannot discriminate anything. Across the cells where the rule stays silent, which is what an analyst acts on, the rate of material error runs from 0.045 to 0.835. On a decision-curve basis every rule in the panel is beaten by scrutinizing every analysis, up to an action threshold of 0.3.
findings: Prespecified verdict: the panel does not classify realized error at the thresholds in use. No rule reached sensitivity 0.80 with specificity 0.50 in every misspecification stratum. ESS below 35 reaches sensitivity 0.251 to 0.326 across strata at specificity 0.909 to 0.926.

The mechanism, which was registered before the run and holds: effective sample size discriminates the outcome-noise component at AUROC 0.847 and the transport component at 0.653, a gap of 0.194. It measures weight dispersion, and weight dispersion is a variance quantity.

The panel is smaller than it looks, by algebra rather than by simulation. ESS, ESS as a percentage and the coefficient of variation of the weights had identical areas under the ROC curve to 0.0e+00 within a fixed source size. The matched-moment balance statistic never exceeded 1.4e-14 and its apparent AUROC of 0.550 is discrimination of floating-point residual, not of balance.

Silence is where the damage is. Across the 88 cells the ESS rule never fires in, the material-error rate runs from 0.045 to 0.835. The registered version of this claim, a spread across the cells it does fire in, was not met (0.150 against a prespecified 0.30) because those cells are all bad; the complementary quantity is stronger and was not prespecified, so it is reported as an observation.

Decision-curve analysis: at action thresholds up to 0.3, flagging every analysis beats every rule in the panel. Only at 0.4 and above does a diagnostic earn its place, and it is the relative effective-sample-size rule rather than the absolute cutoff that gets quoted.

The same statistics work when they measure the actual gap. Pre-weighting imbalance predicts the unadjusted comparison's transport error at AUROC 0.891, against 0.655 for the same statistic applied to MAIC. These diagnostics are informative about the problem and uninformative about the solution: weighting sets to zero the very quantity they measure.

Our proposal, converting residual imbalance on a measured but unadjusted covariate into the units of the estimand with the source-estimated interaction, reaches 0.937 against the transport component in the diagnosable stratum where the best routine diagnostic reaches 0.851. That gain of 0.086 misses the 0.10 we registered, and is reported as a miss.

An adversarial critique of the design before the run found two arithmetic errors in the protocol: the dispersion factor was not the pure variance instrument it was described as wherever the cross-moment channel was on, and the target trial's variance was understated by a factor of two to three. Both were confirmed numerically and corrected before any result was seen.
not_answered: The second half of DIA-03 is untouched: no PSIS-LOO is computed at any hierarchical level and grouped study-level leave-one-out is no more implemented here than in the packages, so the mismatch between the level at which cross-validation is reported and the level at which the prediction is made remains open. DIA-06 is answered only in part; two estimator families and no adjustment are compared on identical replicates, but ML-NMR, NMI, doubly robust estimators and flexible learners are absent. The outcome is continuous with an identity link, which is what buys the exact error decomposition and is also the largest restriction: nothing here transfers to non-collapsible effect measures or time-to-event outcomes, where part of the error is a collapsibility artifact rather than an adjustment failure. Covariates are normal, comparisons are anchored, conditional constancy holds, and target moments are exact. The deployment weights are a declared judgment and nothing in this program measured them, which is why the primary results are within strata.
